lessons.title: Introduction to Flow
lessons.content: Flow is Kotlin's type for asynchronous streams of values, built on coroutines. Real scenario: observing a Room query as Flow<List<Lesson>> that auto-emits on data change.

codeSnippets.code: fun getLessons(): Flow<List<Lesson>> = flow { emit(fetchFromDatabase()) }

lessons.title: Cold Flows
lessons.content: A cold Flow's producer doesn't run until collect() is called, and each collector triggers an independent run. Real scenario: a network-request Flow re-fetching from scratch per new collector.

codeSnippets.code: val numbers = flow { println("Producer started"); emit(1); emit(2) }

lessons.title: Hot Flows
lessons.content: A hot Flow (StateFlow, SharedFlow) is active independent of collectors, shared across multiple collectors. Real scenario: a ViewModel's StateFlow keeps its latest value whether or not anything observes it.

codeSnippets.code:
private val _uiState = MutableStateFlow(UiState.Loading)
val uiState: StateFlow<UiState> = _uiState

lessons.title: flow { } Builder
lessons.content: Creates a Flow by calling emit() inside a suspend lambda, full manual control. Real scenario: wrapping a polling API that emits a new status every few seconds until a job completes.

lessons.title: Flow Operators Overview
lessons.content: Flow supports intermediate operators (map, filter, debounce) and terminal operators (collect, first) that consume it. Real scenario: chaining debounce, filter, map before collecting search results.

codeSnippets.code: searchQuery.debounce(300).filter { it.length >= 2 }.map { it.trim() }.collect { search(it) }

lessons.title: collect (Terminal Operator)
lessons.content: The fundamental terminal operator that starts consuming a Flow - without it, a cold Flow does nothing. Real scenario: a ViewModel collecting a repository Flow to update UI state.

lessons.title: map Operator
lessons.content: Transforms each emitted value into a new value over time. Real scenario: mapping Flow<List<LessonEntity>> into Flow<List<Lesson>> inside a repository.

codeSnippets.code: fun getLessons(id: String) = dao.getLessons(id).map { it.map { e -> e.toDomain() } }

lessons.title: filter Operator
lessons.content: Only lets through emissions matching a predicate. Real scenario: filtering a sensor Flow to only emit readings above a threshold.

codeSnippets.code: sensorFlow.filter { it.value > threshold }.collect { alertUser(it) }

lessons.title: zip Operator (Flow)
lessons.content: Combines the latest paired emissions from two Flows, waiting for both. Real scenario: combining user prefs and feature flags Flows into one config object.

codeSnippets.code: prefsFlow.zip(flagsFlow) { p, f -> Config(p, f) }.collect { applyConfig(it) }

lessons.title: combine Operator
lessons.content: Emits whenever either source Flow emits, using the latest from each. Real scenario: combining search query and filter settings, re-running search whenever either changes.

codeSnippets.code: queryFlow.combine(filtersFlow) { q, f -> SearchRequest(q, f) }.collect { search(it) }

lessons.title: merge Operator
lessons.content: Interleaves emissions from multiple Flows into one stream, in arrival order. Real scenario: merging local DB-change and push-notification event Flows into a single stream.

codeSnippets.code: val allEvents = merge(dbChangesFlow, pushNotificationsFlow)

lessons.title: flatMapConcat
lessons.content: Maps to inner Flows and collects them sequentially, waiting for each to finish. Real scenario: processing an upload queue where each item finishes before the next starts.

codeSnippets.code: uploadQueue.flatMapConcat { uploadFile(it) }.collect { logResult(it) }

lessons.title: flatMapLatest
lessons.content: Maps to inner Flows, cancelling the previous one when a new outer value arrives. Real scenario: search-as-you-type, abandoning an in-flight search on new keystrokes.

codeSnippets.code: searchQuery.debounce(300).flatMapLatest { repository.search(it) }.collect { updateUi(it) }

lessons.title: flatMapMerge
lessons.content: Maps to inner Flows and collects them all concurrently. Real scenario: fetching details for multiple item IDs in parallel, processing each as it arrives.

codeSnippets.code: itemIds.flatMapMerge { fetchItemDetails(it) }.collect { displayItem(it) }

lessons.title: buffer Operator
lessons.content: Lets the emitter run ahead of a slow collector, buffering values instead of throttling to collector speed. Real scenario: a fast sensor-reading Flow while the collector writes slowly to disk.

codeSnippets.code: fastProducerFlow.buffer().collect { slowProcessing(it) }

lessons.title: conflate Operator
lessons.content: Drops intermediate values if the collector is slower, keeping only the latest. Real scenario: a rapidly-updating progress Flow where only the latest percentage matters.

codeSnippets.code: rapidProgressFlow.conflate().collect { updateProgressBar(it) }

lessons.title: debounce Operator
lessons.content: Waits for a quiet period after the last emission before emitting, resetting on new values. Real scenario: waiting 300ms after typing stops before firing a search query.

codeSnippets.code: searchQuery.debounce(300).collect { search(it) }

lessons.title: sample Operator
lessons.content: Periodically emits the most recent value at a fixed interval, discarding the rest. Real scenario: sampling scroll position every 100ms for analytics instead of every pixel change.

codeSnippets.code: scrollPositionFlow.sample(100).collect { logScrollPosition(it) }

lessons.title: retry Operator
lessons.content: Re-subscribes to upstream on exception, up to a specified count or predicate. Real scenario: retrying a flaky network Flow up to 3 times before letting the error propagate.

codeSnippets.code: networkFlow.retry(3) { it is IOException }.catch { emit(fallback) }.collect { updateUi(it) }

lessons.title: retryWhen Operator
lessons.content: Gives full control over retry logic via a predicate receiving cause and attempt count. Real scenario: implementing exponential backoff for a flaky API.

lessons.title: catch Operator
lessons.content: Intercepts exceptions from upstream operators, letting you emit a fallback instead of crashing. Real scenario: catching a network exception and emitting cached data instead.

codeSnippets.code: networkFlow.catch { emit(cachedFallback()) }.collect { updateUi(it) }

lessons.title: StateFlow
lessons.content: Always holds a current value, replays it immediately, conflates rapid updates - built for UI state. Real scenario: HomeViewModel's uiState: StateFlow<HomeUiState> always giving current state instantly.

codeSnippets.code:
private val _uiState = MutableStateFlow<HomeUiState>(Loading)
val uiState: StateFlow<HomeUiState> = _uiState.asStateFlow()

lessons.title: SharedFlow
lessons.content: More configurable, no required initial value, doesn't conflate by default - suited for one-time events. Real scenario: a SharedFlow<UiEvent> emitting one-time snackbar events.

codeSnippets.code:
private val _events = MutableSharedFlow<UiEvent>()
val events: SharedFlow<UiEvent> = _events.asSharedFlow()

lessons.title: StateFlow vs SharedFlow: Choosing Correctly
lessons.content: StateFlow for current state a late collector should see; SharedFlow for one-time events that shouldn't repeat. Real scenario: using StateFlow for events causes navigation to incorrectly re-fire on rotation.

codeSnippets.code:
val uiState: StateFlow<HomeUiState> = _uiState.asStateFlow() // state
val navigationEvents: SharedFlow<NavEvent> = _navEvents.asSharedFlow() // one-time event

lessons.title: channelFlow
lessons.content: Lets you emit from multiple coroutines concurrently into one Flow, backed by a Channel internally. Real scenario: wrapping a callback-based SDK pushing updates from multiple threads.

lessons.title: callbackFlow
lessons.content: Purpose-built for wrapping callback-based APIs as a Flow, with awaitClose for cleanup. Real scenario: wrapping a Firebase snapshot listener as Flow<List<Lesson>>, unregistering on cancellation.
